rows.why: Both docstrings carry the same four-sentence explanatory body word-for-word ('This attribute checks if the status code of the response is between 400 and 600 ... is **not** a check to see if the response code is ``200 OK``.'), diverging only by the trailing ', False if not' on the summary line and a stray comma after 'status code' — a copy-paste of the same explanation onto a second member, where one copy plus a reference would lose nothing.

Same copied-explanation mechanism as the other members of this family: the entire body paragraph about the 400-600 / 200-400 status ranges and the '**not** a check ... ``200 OK``' caveat is reproduced verbatim, with only the ', False if not' clause and one comma distinguishing the two spans.

The two spans are byte-identical over all seven lines, including the identical typo 'If the status code, is between 200 and 400' — a literal duplicated docstring, the strongest possible evidence of copy-paste rather than independent authorship.

The overlap is a mirrored sibling-docstring template — shared opening clause 'Take an object and test to see if it can be represented as a dictionary', the same '::' doctest scaffold with the same three example shapes and the same 'ValueError: cannot encode objects that are not 2-tuples' traceback line, and a ':rtype:' field — while the actual content differs (from_key_val_list returns an OrderedDict, to_key_val_list returns a list of tuples), so neither copy could be deleted.
